correctness.rationale: Fresh check of the repaired theorem: for distinct projective directions the midpoint of the larger gap has equal distances to both nodes of at least pi/4; hence min F≤2^(−p/2). A heaviest node gives max F≥1/2. A single node strictly loses on both bounds. The equal orthogonal pair attains both endpoints by strict convexity of x^(p/2). Its angular mean is c_p, strictly between the endpoints for p>2, so the larger endpoint deviation is the exact optimum. For nonorthogonal nodes both inequalities are strict (gap length and cross contribution or unequal weights). For orthogonal unequal weights the larger weight exceeds 1/2, and at the bisector the derivative is p·2^(−p/2)(1−2w), which proves a strict drop below the bisector value. These strict statements cover any dominant sign and ties without requiring the polarity diagram. The geometric norm identity follows in both directions from surface-area integration and a thin-rectangle sequence with long-side normals at an extremum. The original polarity comparison is also mathematically correct: its Hermite remainder follows by repeated Rolle on [0,1] with differentiability required only in (0,1), where the fourth derivative has fixed sign. In the repaired text the comparison instead follows by averaging the prior order-four moment over phase and comparing with its axis value. The quadratic exact endpoint remains prior context outside the repaired p>2 claim.
residual_risks: The supremum over bodies is obtained as a limit in the proof; full-dimensional attainment is not asserted. Recorded finite diagnostics do not certify the continuum classification.

evidence: The order-four proof shows that H_q(phi)=1/4 sum_k(1+cos(phi+k pi/2))^q has an axis maximum for 1<q<2 and q>3, an axis minimum for 2<q<3, and is constant at q=2,3. It gives H_q(0)=(2^q+2)/4; the uniform phase average is 2^q c_p, with q=p/2. Thus 2c_p−1/2−2^(−q)=2^(1−q)(average H_q−H_q(0)), giving exactly the claimed signs and ties.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: This identity proves that the frozen polarity statement was covered even though the prior theorem is worded for character norms. It says nothing about weights or misaligned normals in the planar competitor class and so does not prove the repaired minimax or its rigidity. Neither the earlier perpendicular-to-node bound for p<2 nor An's spectral exactness theorem implies the sharp nonzero value for p>2.

originality.rationale: The original compound novelty claim fails in a material part: the phase switches at 4 and 6 were advertised as new but are a direct consequence of an earlier inspected order-four moment theorem under averaging. This is verified prior implication, not a mere shared pair of exponents. The repaired claim limits novelty to the minimax formula and unique optimizer for p>2. The closest inspected same-object theorem only gives the subquadratic optimum, whose single perpendicular-to-node obstruction is not useful at p>2. An gives the objective reduction and exactness/endpoint results but no sharp positive two-view superquadratic minimax. The order-four moment analysis concerns phases of a fixed balanced pair and supplies no inequalities or rigidity for arbitrary positive planar two-node rules. Both already-covered components are explicitly credited in the corrected files.
residual_risks: The external discovery query was unavailable; the comparisons concern inspected OA and mirror passages, not exhaustive priority. Classical quadrature sources cited by the follow-up were not independently retrieved. Novelty is restricted to the repaired global minimax statement, not the sign corollary.

value.rationale: The repaired theorem is still a complete sharp design result for a natural regime that complements the known two-view subquadratic result. Even without claiming the switches as new, the exact error and unique rule identify the best performance of the smallest nontrivial positive calibrated directional sampling scheme across continuously varying p. The two universal witnesses and simultaneous equality address competing upper and lower errors, not just an evaluation at a prescribed quadrature.
residual_risks: Value is confined to the stated positive fixed planar at-most-two-direction model, not a larger-node or arbitrary-kernel theorem.
